why: The answer depends on the definition of ecological succession as the gradual, fairly predictable change in species composition of an area ending in a climax (not pioneer) community - a subject no topic in this chapter's list covers.
note: Topic gap: the Ecosystem chapter's topic list has no 'Ecological Succession' topic (pioneer and climax community, hydrarch and xerarch succession, primary vs secondary succession) and offers no 'Unspecified Topic' row either. Its functional topics are productivity, decomposition, energy flow and pyramids, none of which teaches succession, so filing it in any of them would hide the question rather than place it.
